Definition: from G1223 and the base of G5147; to wear through (time), i.e. remain:--abide, be, continue, tarry.
BiblicalUsage: To tarry is to stay on in a place, and Acts uses the word for Paul's long stays in the churches. He tarries long with the disciples at Iconium, he stays at Antioch teaching and preaching, he spends seven days at Troas, and Jesus tarries in Judea with His disciples.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that tarrying is the unglamorous half of mission. Paul did not only arrive and preach; he stayed, and the staying is what turned converts into churches.
